paper.title_en: Exploring the growth-index ($γ$) tension with $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM
paper.abstract_en: Recent analyses have revealed a significant tension in the growth index $γ$. When $γ$ is treated as a free parameter within $Λ$CDM, PL18+$fσ_8$ yields $γ\approx 0.64$, in $\sim4σ$ tension with the expected value $γ\approx 0.55$ (assuming general relativity). We investigate whether $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM -- featuring a rapid sign-switching cosmological constant (mirror AdS-to-dS transition) at redshift $z_\dagger \sim 2$ -- can alleviate the $γ$ tension together with the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions. We find that $γΛ_{\rm s}$CDM can reduce the $γ$ and $H_0$ tensions relative to $γΛ$CDM while maintaining low $S_8$ values. For PL18+$fσ_8$, it yields $z_\dagger>1.58$ (95% CL) and reduces the $γ$ and $H_0$ discrepancies from $3.7σ$ and $4.2σ$ in $γΛ$CDM to $2.1σ$ and $1.1σ$, with $χ^2_{\rm min}$ essentially unchanged. The largest improvement among the free-$z_\dagger$ analyses is for PL18+$fσ_8$+PP&SH0ES, with $z_\dagger=1.82^{+0.32}_{-0.28}$ (95% CL), $γ$ and $H_0$ tensions of $1.8σ$ and $0.6σ$, and an improved fit. The efficacy is, however, dataset dependent: the 3D BAO measurements from SDSS-IV/eBOSS and the first year of DESI observations tend to push the transition to $z_\dagger\gtrsim2.3$--$2.4$ and weaken the simultaneous alleviation, particularly of the $H_0$ tension. The fixed-$z_\dagger=1.7$ benchmark yields low residual tensions for PL18 and PL18+$fσ_8$, albeit with somewhat worse fits than $γΛ$CDM, but is excluded at more than $2σ$ by the free-$z_\dagger$ analyses once the uncalibrated PantheonPlus SN Ia sample or the 3D BAO data are included. Our results indicate that $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM can contribute to the joint alleviation of multiple cosmological tensions, although its impact is dataset dependent.
